chapter.title: Data Science
chapter.para: numpy, matplotlib and pandas are what many people come to Python for. They are installed apart from Python (pip install numpy matplotlib pandas), in the Python that Rexx uses.

section.title: numpy Arrays
section.para: How it works. Rexx's operators on a Python object are Python's, so a * 10 multiplies every element, and a > 2 is an array of truth values, a boolean mask, which selects elements in a[a > 2]. The Python object must be on the left: 10 * a would be Rexx's arithmetic. m[1, 0] is numpy's m[1, 0], row 1, column 0, from 0. numpy's scalars come back as Rexx strings, like Python's numbers.

section.title: A Chart
section.para: You want a chart, saved as an image.

How it works. The Agg backend draws without a screen, into a file. .py~import("matplotlib.pyplot") is the pyplot module. Keyword arguments, label=, go with .py~kw, and 2 * np~pi is Rexx's arithmetic on numpy's π, which comes back as a Rexx string.

section.title: A pandas DataFrame
section.para: You want a table: new columns, selections, groups.

How it works. A column is df["sales"], and Rexx's operators on it are pandas': df["sales"] * 0.21 is a new column, and df["sales"] > 100 a boolean mask that selects rows. drop gives a new DataFrame (pandas 3.1 deprecates inplace=). index= of to_string is annotated as a bool in pandas, so .false, the Rexx string 0, goes to it as False: the bridge reads the annotation of the parameter a 1 or a 0 goes to. DO OVER the index of a grouped Series gives its labels.
